description: Comilla University team & NASA Space Apps 2025 Global Finalist tackling "Abandoned but not Forgotten." We are building an interactive scrollytelling platform bringing NASA's retired Moon and Mars equipment to life using open data, archival imagery, and telemetry. Skilled in web engineering, UI/UX, and data integration. Seeking collaborators passionate about creative writing, storytelling, and digital visualization.

SPACE GHOSTS
A Bilingual Time-Travel Learning Adventure Through NASA's Forgotten Machines
Space Ghosts is a free, bilingual (English and বাংলা) web application designed for children aged 10–15. It tells the stories of 17 NASA machines left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.

The adventure begins at Mission Control in 2026, travels back to 1964, and then moves forward through history. Along the way, children discover each machine through an engaging seven-part illustrated story, accompanied by a Mission File containing five verified NASA facts.

For every machine, readers can:
- Explore a seven-part illustrated story.
- Discover five verified facts through its Mission File.
- Listen to read-aloud narration in their preferred language.
- Take a ten-question Star Quiz.
- Rebuild the machine through an interactive 3×3 jigsaw puzzle.
The platform includes 119 stories and 170 quiz questions in both English and Bengali, creating an engaging combination of storytelling, science, history, and interactive learning.

A friendly panda professor, Prof. Pandastein, guides children throughout their journey and answers their questions.

The entire application runs directly in the browser, with no backend, no login, and no user tracking. Its lightweight design makes it suitable for school tablets and environments with slow internet connections.
details:
SPACE GHOSTS

A Bilingual Time-Travel Learning Adventure Through NASA's Forgotten Machines

Project Overview | Educational Technology | Interactive Space Exploration

Explore the past. Discover forgotten machines. Experience the history of space exploration.

1. Introduction

Space Ghosts is a bilingual (English and বাংলা), story-driven, time-travel learning adventure designed for children aged 10–15. It brings to life the stories of 17 NASA machines left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.

The adventure begins at Mission Control in 2026, travels backward in time to 1964, and then moves forward through history until 2021. Along this journey, readers encounter each machine in chronological order, discovering its mission, scientific purpose, journey, achievements, and eventual fate.

Rather than treating these machines as forgotten pieces of hardware, Space Ghosts gives each one a story worth remembering.

2. How the Experience Works

Every machine offers a complete educational journey through a seven-part illustrated story, combining narrative storytelling, scientific information, interactive activities, and educational challenges.

2.1 What Each Machine Includes

Seven-Part Illustrated Story

A detailed narrative exploring the machine's background, mission, journey, discoveries, and eventual fate.

Mission File

Five verified facts about the machine and its mission.

Read-Aloud Narration

Audio narration available in the reader's selected language.

Star Quiz

A ten-question quiz designed to test and reinforce understanding.

3 × 3 Jigsaw Puzzle

An interactive puzzle that makes learning more engaging and enjoyable.

2.2 Overall Learning Experience

  • Total Machines: 17 NASA machines
  • Illustrated Stories: 119 stories
  • Quiz Questions: 170 questions in two languages
  • Languages: English and Bengali (বাংলা)
  • Platform: Browser-based application
  • Backend: No backend required
  • User Authentication: No login required
  • User Tracking: No user tracking

2.3 Meet Prof. Pandastein

Guiding readers throughout their journey is Prof. Pandastein, a panda professor who serves as the adventure's educational companion.

Prof. Pandastein introduces the machines, explains scientific concepts, provides historical context, and answers readers' questions. His character makes complex scientific ideas more approachable and gives the experience a friendly, consistent personality.

Importantly, Space Ghosts puts readers in control.

Nothing automatically plays or speaks. Every narration, activity, and interaction begins only when the reader chooses it.

3. The Challenge We Address

"Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling About NASA's Discarded Equipment"

Space Ghosts explores an important question:

What happens to the machines we leave behind when their missions are over?

Space exploration is often remembered through historic launches, famous astronauts, scientific discoveries, and distant worlds. Yet many of the machines that made these achievements possible remain on the Moon, on Mars, or in deep space long after their missions have ended.

Space Ghosts brings these overlooked objects back into the story.

Instead of presenting abandoned spacecraft as simple historical artefacts, the project treats each machine as a character with its own journey, purpose, achievements, and ending.

Readers discover the people, engineering, scientific achievements, and historical events behind each machine.

By the end of every journey, readers understand five essential aspects of its story:

Purpose

What the machine was designed to do.

Journey

Where it travelled and how it reached its destination.

Science

What scientific purpose it served and what it helped humanity discover.

Ending

How its mission ended and what happened to the machine.

Legacy

What remains of it today and why its story matters.

3.1 Five Different Endings

Every machine receives an ending classification, represented through a distinct visual identity using colour, shape, and a descriptive name.

Crashed on Purpose

Deliberately impacted a celestial body or was intentionally deorbited.

At Rest on the Moon

Left on the lunar surface.

Gone Quiet

Lost communication or became inactive.

Retired

Its mission was officially concluded.

Still Talking

Continues transmitting or communicating.

The visual system uses multiple indicators rather than relying on colour alone. This improves accessibility and helps readers understand each classification more easily.

3.2 Learning to Verify Information

Scientific accuracy and source transparency are central to Space Ghosts.

The project credits the NASA origins of its stories, images, and scientific information. Its principal reference sources include:

  • NASA National Space Science Data Center (NSSDCA)
  • NASA Science
  • NASA Photojournal
  • NASA Moon Trek
  • IAU 2015 lunar coordinate framework

Editorial Transparency

The project also openly documents areas requiring further research and verification.

  • Items Requiring Verification: 33
  • Known Conflicts: 8

Rather than hiding uncertainty, Space Ghosts makes source verification part of the educational experience.

It encourages children to question information, examine evidence, compare sources, and understand why reliable scientific references matter.

This approach introduces an important scientific principle: learning is not simply about collecting facts; it is also about understanding how those facts are established.

4. What We Would Build Next

The next development phase will focus on expanding scientific exploration, introducing immersive interactive experiences, improving accessibility, and making Space Ghosts more useful in educational environments.

4.1 Planned Development Features

1. Interactive Lunar Terrain and Spacecraft Exploration

Develop an interactive 3D exploration experience for the Ranger 7 mission, featuring an inspectable spacecraft model and a scientifically reconstructed representation of its actual lunar impact site.

The experience will include five educational hotspots covering:

  • Cameras
  • Solar Panels
  • High-Gain Antenna
  • Omni Antenna
  • Spacecraft Structure

Each hotspot will explain the function and engineering significance of the relevant spacecraft component.

The lunar landscape will be reconstructed using NASA's scientific datasets, including:

  • Elevation Source: NASA Moon Trek / LRO LOLA
  • DEM Dataset: LRO_LOLA_DEM_Global_256ppd_v06
  • Elevation Resolution: 256 pixels per degree (ppd)
  • Terrain Dimensions: 512 × 512
  • Spatial Resolution: 46.48 m/px
  • Total Elevation Relief: 937.76 m
  • Terrain Coverage: 23.8 km tile
  • Colour Imagery: LRO WAC Global Mosaic
  • Imagery Resolution: 303 ppd
  • Location: Mare Cognitum
  • Coordinates: 10.70° S, 20.612° W

The terrain will also feature historically calculated solar illumination based on the Sun's position on 31 July 1964, the date of the Ranger 7 impact.

This will provide an educational environment grounded in actual lunar geography rather than a generic representation of the Moon.

The experience will also include a dedicated presentation of the historic A001 image, connecting the interactive exploration with the historical achievement of the Ranger 7 mission.

2. Mars Landing and Resting Site Reconstructions

Develop interactive 3D reconstructions of the resting places of four historic Mars missions:

  • Opportunity
  • InSight
  • Phoenix
  • Viking 1

Using NASA Mars Trek elevation and colour datasets, these experiences will extend terrain-based exploration from the Moon to Mars.

Children will be able to explore the landscapes surrounding these historic missions and better understand the places where their journeys ended.

The goal is to bring the geography and history of Mars exploration to life through scientifically grounded interactive environments.

3. Sources & Credits Screen

Create a dedicated reference section listing NASA URLs and dataset identifiers associated with individual stories, quiz questions, images, and interactive features.

This will make scientific references easier to access, examine, and verify.

It will also strengthen the project's commitment to transparency, research, and scientific accuracy.

4. Offline Mode and Android Packaging

Introduce service-worker-based offline functionality and package the application using Capacitor.

The goal is to make Space Ghosts accessible on low-end Android tablets, including in educational environments where reliable internet connectivity is limited.

This will help bring the experience to schools, libraries, and communities with limited access to high-speed internet.

5. More Languages and Classroom Resources

Expand the language offering beyond English and Bengali while introducing additional resources designed to support classroom learning.

4.2 Planned Languages and Educational Additions

Spanish Translation

Reach Spanish-speaking learners and expand international accessibility.

Hindi Translation

Make the experience accessible to more learners across South Asia and beyond.

Arabic Translation

Extend the educational experience to Arabic-speaking audiences.

Teacher's Sheet

Support classroom activities, guided learning, and educational discussions.

These additions will help Space Ghosts reach a wider international audience while supporting its adoption in schools, libraries, and other educational environments.

5. Our Vision

Space Ghosts is more than a collection of stories about old spacecraft.

It is an attempt to connect history, science, storytelling, and interactive technology to help a new generation understand humanity's exploration of space.

Every abandoned machine has a story worth remembering.

Every mission represents human curiosity, engineering, courage, and discovery.

The machines may have stopped working, lost contact, or remained where their missions ended. But their contributions to science and human exploration have not disappeared.

Through bilingual storytelling, interactive educational activities, scientific datasets, historical imagery, and future immersive exploration experiences, Space Ghosts aims to make the history of space exploration accessible, memorable, and exciting for children.

Our goal is simple:

To make children feel that they are not just reading about space history — they are travelling through it.

SPACE GHOSTS — Every Machine Has a Story. Every Mission Leaves a Legacy.
